title: The Letter of Jude Timeline
sub: Contend for the Faith · A Letter Changed at the Last Minute
desc: A one-chapter letter Jude says he changed at the last minute, from a general essay on salvation into an urgent warning against intruders twisting grace into license — closing in one of the New Testament's most quoted doxologies.

eras.label: Era One · Jude 1
eras.name: Contend for the Faith
eras.dates: A one-chapter letter, changed at the last minute from a general essay on salvation into an urgent warning about intruders already inside the church

events.title: Greeting — A Letter Changed at the Last Minute
events.detail: Jude, identifying himself only as James's brother, explains he'd planned to write about their shared salvation but felt compelled instead to urge readers to contend earnestly for a faith already handed down once for all.

verses.text: “While I was making every effort to write you about our common salvation, I felt the necessity to write to you exhorting that you contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all handed down to the saints.”

events.title: Certain Persons Have Crept In — Egypt, Fallen Angels, Sodom
events.detail: Jude names the crisis directly — ungodly people have infiltrated the church, twisting grace into license — and stacks three Old Testament precedents of judgment: Israel destroyed in the wilderness, angels bound in darkness, and Sodom and Gomorrah's example of eternal fire.

verses.text: “Certain persons have crept in unnoticed… ungodly persons who turn the grace of our God into sensuality and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.”

events.title: Cain, Balaam, Korah — and Enoch's Ancient Prophecy
events.detail: A vivid, image-dense denunciation of the intruders as waterless clouds, fruitless trees, and wild sea-foam — compared to Cain, Balaam, and Korah, and judged in advance by a prophecy attributed to Enoch, quoted directly from a text outside the Hebrew Bible.

verses.text: “They have gone the way of Cain, and for pay they have poured themselves into the error of Balaam, and perished in the rebellion of Korah.”

“Enoch, in the seventh generation from Adam, also prophesied about these men, saying, ‘Behold, the Lord came with many thousands of His holy ones, to execute judgment upon all.’” — quoting 1 Enoch, a Jewish text outside the Hebrew canon, as genuine prophecy.

events.title: Remember the Apostles' Words — Build Yourselves Up, Show Mercy
events.detail: Against the mockers the apostles had already predicted, Jude calls believers to build themselves up in faith and prayer, staying in God's love while actively rescuing others — some through doubt, some snatched directly from the fire.

verses.text: “On some, who are doubting, have mercy; and for others, save, snatching them out of the fire.”

events.title: Able to Keep You From Stumbling — The Closing Doxology
events.detail: One of the most quoted benedictions in the New Testament closes the letter — confidence not in the readers' own strength against the threats just described, but in the God able to keep them from falling and present them blameless with joy.

verses.text: “To Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, and to make you stand in the presence of His glory blameless with great joy… be glory, majesty, might, and authority, before all time and now and forever. Amen.”
